## Local development profile

The complete stack runs locally against the released Nox Docker images — this is the same
environment the [quick start](/docs/quickstart) uses and the judged demo's fallback:

```bash
pnpm test:integration   # boots Handle Gateway, KMS, ingestor, JetStream, Runner
```

The Hardhat Nox plugin manages the containers; contracts deploy fresh each run, so the local
profile needs no address table.

# Architecture
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/architecture
The immutable contract stack — ballot core, eligibility strategies, Safe module, compatible Governor, and the versioned factory that deploys them.

Every production contract is immutable: no owner, no proxy, no upgrade path. A versioned
factory deploys complete stacks and emits full code-hash evidence, so what you verified is
what runs.

<Mermaid
  chart={`
flowchart TB
    F["ConfidentialGovernanceFactory<br/>version 1 - pinned creation-code hashes"]

    subgraph SAFE["Safe path"]
        S["Official Safe 1.5.0"] -- enableModule --> M["SafeConfidentialVotingModule"]
        M -- constructs --> C1["ConfidentialBallotCore"]
        M -- "batch actions via delegatecall" --> MS["Official MultiSendCallOnly"]
    end

    subgraph GOV["Governor path"]
        G["ConfidentialGovernor<br/>OpenZeppelin 5.6.1"] -- constructs --> C2["ConfidentialBallotCore"]
        G -- "queue / execute" --> T["TimelockController"]
    end

    F -- deploySafeModule --> M
    F -- deployGovernor --> G
    F -- "deploys once, shared" --> E["IVotesSnapshotStrategy<br/>MerkleWeightedAllowlistStrategy"]
    C1 -- "encrypted operations" --> N["NoxCompute<br/>confidential compute + ACL"]
    C2 -- "encrypted operations" --> N
    E -.-> C1
    E -.-> C2
`}
/>

## The pieces

- **ConfidentialBallotCore** — adapter-owned; each host constructs its own. Holds the
  committed ballot rules, enforces eligibility and sequence/replacement law, runs the
  encrypted accounting, requests the tally, and finalizes the verdict from Gateway evidence.
  Every persistent Nox ACL grant targets the core itself — never a viewer.
- **Eligibility strategies** — public eligibility and first-cast weight only:
  `IVotesSnapshotStrategy` (token voting power at a snapshot) and
  `MerkleWeightedAllowlistStrategy` (a domain-separated weighted allowlist; each leaf binds
  chain, host, snapshot, voter, and weight).
- **SafeConfidentialVotingModule** — immutably bound to one Safe, one core, and the official
  `MultiSendCallOnly`. Registration is Safe-only; execution is permissionless, exact,
  and execute-once with rollback-safe retry.
- **ConfidentialGovernor** — composes OpenZeppelin `Governor` with every plaintext cast route
  disabled. Truthful detailed states (`TallyPending`, `Withheld`, …) alongside the standard
  enum; Passed proposals queue through a real `TimelockController`.
- **Factory** — publishes contract/rules version 1, pins the reviewed creation-code hashes,
  revalidates every shared dependency's runtime hash before CREATE, and emits complete
  address + code-hash evidence per deployment.

## Verified behavior

The local gate behind these docs: **119 Forge tests**, a stateful invariant profile of
**960,000 modeled calls** (one effective weight per voter, floor monotonicity, finalize-once,
execute-once, exact action binding), a released-stack proof-negative matrix (wrong signer,
domain, handle, encoding, replay — all reject independently), and **33/33** consecutive
released Docker-stack cases including Runner restart and JetStream redelivery recovery.

---

# How it works
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/how-it-works
Five lifecycle stages, what becomes public at each, and why only one value ever reaches the public record.

Every ballot operation moves through five stages. What becomes public at each step: your
wallet, your voting weight, and the time you acted. Your choice is not among them, at any
stage.

<Mermaid
  chart={`
sequenceDiagram
    participant V as Voter wallet
    participant G as Handle Gateway (attested)
    participant C as Ballot core (on-chain)
    participant N as Nox confidential compute

    V->>G: Encoded choice (For / Against / Abstain)
    G-->>V: Encrypted handle + input proof
    V->>C: castVote(ballotId, sequence, handle, proof, eligibility)
    Note over C: Public record - wallet, weight, time.<br/>Never the choice.
    C->>N: Fold operation into sealed totals
    N-->>C: Recorded (status only)
    Note over C,N: After close, above the privacy floor
    C->>N: requestTally - permissionless
    N-->>C: One encrypted boolean verdict
    N-->>C: Gateway-signed decryption proof
    C->>C: finalize() - Passed or Rejected, once
`}
/>

## The five stages

1. **Preparing encrypted handle** — the SDK sends your encoded choice to the attested Handle
   Gateway, which encrypts it and returns a handle and proof. The Gateway sees the input; this
   is inside the declared trust boundary, and we say so plainly.
2. **Ready for wallet** — the transaction is assembled, waiting for your signature.
3. **Submitting** — the transaction goes on-chain. It contains the opaque handle, not your
   choice. Your wallet and the time are now public.
4. **Confidential computation** — Nox folds the operation into the sealed totals. No progress
   figure is shown, because none is knowable.
5. **Recorded** — a receipt confirms the operation status. Only an eligible wallet's newest
   effective Recorded operation counts.

## Replacement, floor, and the reveal

Before close you may replace your vote up to two times (`sequence` 1 → 2 → 3). The newest
accepted operation counts; a replacement never increases the unique-wallet count. Abstain is a
real participation choice, and any non-canonical encrypted value is deterministically
normalized to Abstain — there is no hidden validity class.

At close, anyone may request the tally. Two rules then apply, in order:

- Below the **privacy floor** (unique Recorded wallets), the result is **withheld** —
  terminally, with no Nox call and no verdict handle at all.
- At or above it, the core derives exactly one encrypted boolean — governance quorum met and
  For weight above Against weight — and grants public decryption to that handle **only**.

The contract accepts the configured Gateway's signed evidence for the exact stored verdict
handle, validates encoding, domain, and replay, and finalizes **Passed** or **Rejected** once.
Exact totals are not disclosed. Ever.

---

# Overview
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs
What NoxVote is, what stays private, what stays public, and what is deliberately not promised.

NoxVote turns on confidential voting for sensitive governance. Members' wallets and
participation stay public, their For/Against/Abstain choices never appear on-chain or become
public, and only the final Passed/Rejected verdict is revealed — after enough eligible wallets
recorded operations. A Passed verdict can execute the exact Safe or Governor action everyone
reviewed before voting.

It is not a standalone DAO app. It is a **host-neutral confidential ballot core** with two
production adapters: a Safe module (retrofit an existing Safe with a normal owner-threshold
transaction) and a compatible OpenZeppelin Governor (native governance-framework integration
with a real TimelockController).

## Public and private, exactly

| Always public | Never public |
| --- | --- |
| Your wallet address | Your choice |
| Your voting weight | Anyone else's choice |
| That you participated, and when | Exact option totals |
| Operation status (Submitted / Computing / Recorded) | Intermediate encrypted values |
| The committed action, rules, and dates | — |
| The final verdict (above the privacy floor) | — |

Two rules are committed before voting opens and never merged:

- The **privacy floor** decides whether *any* result may be disclosed at all. Below it, the
  outcome is **Result withheld** — no verdict, no totals, no manual release, nothing executes.
  That is a designed outcome, not a failure.
- The **governance quorum** decides whether the proposal passes, following the host's rule.

## Where to go

- [Quick start](/docs/quickstart) — run the full flow on the released local Nox stack.
- [How it works](/docs/how-it-works) — the five lifecycle stages and the verdict-only reveal.
- [Architecture](/docs/architecture) — the immutable contract stack.
- [Integrate](/docs/integrate/deploy) — deploy through the versioned factory.
- [Honest limits](/docs/limits) — what this does **not** promise. Read it before you rely on
  any claim above.

---

# Deploy the contracts
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/integrate/deploy
Deploy a complete confidential voting stack through the versioned factory, with pinned creation-code hashes and full on-chain evidence.

All production deployment goes through **`ConfidentialGovernanceFactory`** (contract/rules
version 1). The factory owns one reviewed instance of each eligibility strategy, pins the
exact reviewed creation-code hashes for everything it deploys, and revalidates every shared
dependency's runtime code hash before any CREATE. If anything drifted, deployment reverts
before a single contract exists.

## Safe stack

```solidity
function deploySafeModule(
    address safe,
    uint32 organizationMinimumPrivacyFloor,
    bytes calldata safeModuleCreationCode
) external returns (SafeConfidentialVotingModule module, ConfidentialBallotCore core);
```

You supply the module creation bytecode; the factory accepts it only if it hashes to the
pinned `SAFE_MODULE_CREATION_CODE_HASH`. One call creates a distinct immutable module whose
constructor creates its own Safe-bound core, then emits `SafeModuleDeployed` with the
version, every address (Safe, module, core, both strategies, `MultiSendCallOnly`), the
organization privacy floor, and every code hash.

## Governor stack

```solidity
function deployGovernor(
    GovernorDeploymentConfig calldata config, // token, settings, quorum, floor, timelock delay
    bytes calldata governorCreationCode,
    bytes calldata timelockCreationCode
) external returns (ConfidentialGovernor governor, TimelockController timelock, ConfidentialBallotCore core);
```

One atomic call deploys the `TimelockController`, the immutable Governor, and the
Governor-owned core; grants **only the Governor** proposer/canceller authority; opens
execution through the zero-address executor role; verifies timelock self-administration; and
renounces (and verifies removal of) the factory's temporary admin. Deployment events bind the
complete configuration hash plus creation- and runtime-code evidence.

## After deployment

Compare the emitted code hashes against your own build of the reviewed source, then record
the addresses. The live Ethereum Sepolia deployment — every contract, with explorer links — is
on the [Deployed addresses](/docs/addresses) page.

---

# Governor path
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/integrate/governor
A compatible OpenZeppelin Governor whose only voting route is confidential, with truthful async states and a real TimelockController.

`ConfidentialGovernor` composes OpenZeppelin 5.6.1 `Governor`, `GovernorSettings`,
`GovernorVotes`, `GovernorVotesQuorumFraction`, and `GovernorTimelockControl` around an
adapter-owned ballot core. It is deployed complete and immutable by the
[factory](/docs/integrate/deploy), which wires the timelock roles and renounces admin.

## Propose

```solidity
function proposeConfidential(
    address[] memory targets,
    uint256[] memory values,
    bytes[] memory calldatas,
    string memory description,
    uint32 privacyFloor
) public returns (uint256 proposalId, bytes32 ballotId);
```

`proposeConfidential` reproduces OpenZeppelin's proposer checks, creates a normal one- or
multi-action proposal, then **atomically** registers its token snapshot, schedule, and action
commitment in the core. If core registration fails, the Governor proposal rolls back.

## What is deliberately disabled

- Standard `propose` — every proposal must be confidential.
- All five public plaintext cast routes, both internal cast overloads, and `_countVote` —
  there is no plaintext ballot path to fall back to. Signature-based rejections do not
  consume nonces.
- Standard `cancel` — replaced by `cancelConfidential`, which allows the proposer to cancel
  only while the ballot is still Scheduled and cancels Governor and core atomically.

## Truthful states

The detailed getter reports the real lifecycle: `Scheduled`, `Open`, `Closed`,
`TallyPending`, `Withheld`, `Rejected`, `Passed`, `Queued`, `Executed`, `Canceled`. Standard
Governor clients see the closest honest standard value — a closed-but-unresolved proposal
reads `Pending` (never a premature `Succeeded`), `Withheld`/`Rejected` map to `Defeated`,
`Passed` maps to `Succeeded`. Third-party Governor UIs may misread the compatibility
`Pending` state; the detailed state is the truth.

## Execution

A finalized Passed proposal queues through the real `TimelockController` with the configured
delay, exposes its exact ETA, and executes permissionlessly at the ETA — standard OpenZeppelin
governance semantics, driven by a confidential verdict instead of a public tally.

---

# Safe path
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/integrate/safe
Retrofit an existing Safe with confidential voting - enable the module, register a committed proposal, and let anyone execute the Passed verdict exactly once.

The Safe path is a retrofit: an official Safe 1.5.0 enables the deployed module through a
normal owner-threshold transaction. No migration, no new wallet, no change to your owners.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Enable the module

From the Safe, execute `enableModule(module)`. The module's `isInstalled()` flips true. The
module is immutably bound to this one Safe at construction — it cannot be pointed elsewhere.

</Step>
<Step>

### Register a proposal (Safe-only)

```solidity
function registerProposal(
    SafeAction[] calldata actions,          // exact ordered (to, value, data) bundle
    SafeBallotConfig calldata ballotConfig  // eligibility, dates, quorum, floor, replacements
) external onlySafe returns (bytes32 safeProposalId, bytes32 ballotId);
```

Registration is a Safe transaction, so it carries your normal owner threshold. The module
derives a nonce-separated proposal ID, commits the hash of the exact ordered action bundle in
both the module and the core, and stores the absolute governance quorum. Everything is fixed
when the record opens — action, dates, snapshot, quorum, passage rule, privacy floor,
replacement limit — and unchangeable afterwards.

</Step>
<Step>

### Execute the verdict (anyone)

```solidity
function execute(bytes32 safeProposalId, SafeAction[] calldata actions) external;
```

Execution requires the core's final **Passed** result and a recomputed action hash identical
to registration — altered target, value, data, or order rejects before any call. A single
action executes as a direct Call; multiple actions pack through the official
`MultiSendCallOnly` (runtime code hash revalidated at execution time), where one failing
inner action rolls back the whole bundle. The proposal is consumed before the external call —
reentrancy and replay are blocked — and a failed Safe execution rolls the flag back for an
exact retry. The Safe owner nonce is never consumed.

</Step>
</Steps>

Withheld, Rejected, and unresolved proposals cannot execute anything, and there is no
plaintext fallback or administrator override anywhere in the path.

---

# Honest limits
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/limits
What NoxVote deliberately does not promise, and who you are trusting, named in full.

Several of these are achievable, and some are ahead of us. None of them are what the module
does today, so none of them are claimed today.

## Not promised

- **Client-side encryption.** The released SDK sends your encoded choice to iExec's attested
  Handle Gateway, which encrypts it and returns the handle. The Gateway sees the input during
  preparation. Nothing is encrypted in your browser, and we do not say it is.
- **Anonymity.** Your wallet, your weight, your participation, and your replacement timing
  are all on-chain and linkable. Only the choice is withheld.
- **Receipt-freeness.** Nothing here stops you from proving to someone else how you voted, if
  you decide to. MACI prevents convincing receipts through a hidden authenticated key/command
  state; released Nox does not supply that mechanism.
- **Bribe resistance.** Replacement voting raises the cost of buying a vote — the last
  accepted operation counts — but a coercer can still supervise the final action.
- **A full tally proof.** The accepted evidence is a Gateway signature over a decryption, not
  a proof of the computation or the complete private operation history.
- **Threshold key custody.** The released Nox stack uses **one KMS node holding the full
  private key**. That is weaker than a threshold committee, where no single operator can
  decrypt alone. It belongs here, not in a footnote.

## Trusted today, named

1. The Handle Gateway, which sees the input before it is sealed.
2. The Nox TEE stack that performs the confidential computation.
3. The single-node KMS holding the decryption key.
4. The Gateway signer whose signature the evidence rests on.
5. The deployed module code, which binds proposal, type, and replay.

## What still holds

Within that boundary, the load-bearing property survives: individual choices and exact totals
never appear on-chain, are never published afterwards, and are never opened per-ballot at the
end — unlike shielded-voting designs that reveal every ballot after close. Disclosure is one
boolean, gated by a privacy floor, bound to one committed action.

---

# Quick start
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/quickstart
Run the complete confidential ballot — four wallets, one replacement, a sealed tally, one public verdict — on the released local Nox stack.

The judged demo story runs end to end on your machine against the **released** Nox Docker
stack: Handle Gateway, KMS, ingestor, JetStream, and Runner. Nothing is mocked.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22–24 and pnpm
- Docker (running)
- [Foundry](https://getfoundry.sh) (`forge` on your PATH)

## Run it

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install and verify the contracts

```bash
pnpm install
forge test        # 119 tests, full suite green
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Run the full confidential flow

```bash
pnpm test:integration
```

The Hardhat Nox plugin boots the released Docker stack, then proves the whole story: four
weighted Merkle-eligible wallets encrypt choices through the Handle Gateway and cast them,
one voter replaces a vote twice (Against → Abstain → For), the ballot closes at privacy floor
four, anyone requests the tally, and the core finalizes **Passed** from the Gateway's signed
decryption proof — while every submitted ballot handle stays non-public.

</Step>
<Step>

### Read the record

The test asserts what the demo claims: recorded participation is public (4 wallets, weight
10), no submitted handle is ever publicly decryptable, no viewer grant is emitted, and exactly
one handle — the verdict — is marked publicly decryptable. Warm close-to-proof time is under
0.6 seconds; the full path takes about 15 seconds.

</Step>
</Steps>

## What just happened

Choices were encrypted **before** the wallet transaction, so the public chain carries only
opaque handles. The tally runs inside Nox's confidential compute; only one encrypted boolean —
"did For outweigh Against?" — was ever allowed to become public. See
[How it works](/docs/how-it-works) for each stage, and
[Verify a result](/docs/verification) for exactly what the proof checks.

---

# Verify a result
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/verification
What the decryption proof actually checks, what module state binds, and what you can independently inspect on-chain.

A confidentiality claim is only as good as what you can check. Here is exactly what the
evidence proves — and what it does not.

## What the proof checks

Finalization accepts one piece of evidence: the configured Gateway signer's EIP-712 signature
over the **exact verdict handle stored for that proposal** and its decrypted boolean result
(domain: `NoxCompute`, the chain ID, the NoxCompute contract). The core validates:

- the signature recovers to the configured Gateway signer;
- the handle is the one expected verdict handle stored at tally request — no other handle is
  accepted;
- the decrypted payload is a canonical boolean (`0x00`/`0x01`, exactly one byte);
- the chain domain matches — foreign-chain and foreign-host evidence rejects;
- finalization happens exactly once.

Short, mutated, wrong-signer, wrong-domain, wrong-handle, malformed-length, and
non-canonical-boolean evidence each reject independently, leaving the state unchanged.

## What module state binds

The proposal's committed action hash, dates, snapshot, quorum, privacy floor, and replacement
rule are immutable from registration. The verdict handle is derived from the ballot's
domain-separated ID, so identical encrypted inputs on two proposals still produce different
expected verdict handles — cross-proposal and cross-host replay cannot work.

## What you can inspect on-chain

- **ACL evidence**: every submitted ballot handle remains non-public
  (`isPubliclyDecryptable == false`), no viewer grant is ever emitted, and exactly one handle
  — the verdict — is marked publicly decryptable, by the core, after close.
- **Participation**: recorded unique wallets and weight, against the committed floor and
  quorum.
- **Execution match**: the executed Safe/Governor action recomputes to the registered action
  hash. Anything altered rejects.

## What the proof is not

It is a Gateway signature over a decryption, **not** a SNARK over the tally arithmetic or the
full private operation history. Proposal binding, expected type, and execute-once behavior
come from module state; trust in the computation itself rests on the parties named in the
trust boundary. Read [Honest limits](/docs/limits) — that page is part of this one.

---

# Voter guide
URL: https://docs.noxvote.xyz/docs/voters
What you see, what you sign, what becomes public, and how vote replacement works.

## Eligibility and weight

Eligibility and voting weight are public, resolved by the ballot's committed strategy: either
token voting power at the committed snapshot (IVotes) or a weighted allowlist whose Merkle
leaves bind chain, host, snapshot, your wallet, and your weight. Your weight is **fixed at
your first cast** — later token movements do not change it.

## Casting

You choose For, Against, or Abstain. The SDK sends the encoded choice to the attested Handle
Gateway, which encrypts it and returns the handle and proof your wallet transaction carries:

```ts
const { handle, handleProof } = await handleClient.encryptInput(choice, 'uint16', core)
await core.castVote(ballotId, sequence, handle, handleProof, eligibilityProof)
```

The public transaction contains the opaque handle — never your choice. Your operation then
moves **Submitted → Computing → Recorded**, and the receipt you get back confirms *status*,
not your plaintext choice. No progress percentage is ever shown, because none is knowable.

Every representable input is a defined choice: any value other than the canonical
For/Against/Abstain encodings is deterministically normalized to **Abstain**. There is no
hidden "invalid ballot" class that could leak information later.

## Replacing your vote

<Mermaid
  chart={`
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    s1: Cast (sequence 1)
    s2: Replacement (sequence 2)
    s3: Replacement (sequence 3)
    [*] --> s1
    s1 --> s2: before close
    s2 --> s3: before close
    s3 --> [*]: newest Recorded counts
`}
/>

Before close you may replace your vote up to **two times**, in strict sequence. The newest
accepted operation is the one that counts; the encrypted accounting removes your previous
contribution and adds the new one without either becoming public. Replacement is a
coercion-recovery window — the fact and timing of your replacement are public, its content is
not.

## What counts toward the privacy floor

Unique eligible wallets whose **newest effective operation is Recorded**. Abstain counts.
Replacements do not add a second participant. Pending, failed, rejected, and stale operations
do not count. You always see participation progress against the floor — never a running
tally, never a projected winner.
